policy: Ten independent console ports. Metadata and CI validation never imply hardware compatibility. Source builds, kernel boot, userspace, graphics and physical hardware are separate evidence gates. CI performs host-side source builds only; no firmware modification, exploit execution, payload deployment or physical-console writes.

targets.name: Sony PlayStation Portable
targets.toolchain_strategy: MIPS little-endian cross-toolchain; ABI and kernel config audit
targets.desktop_goal: Slackware-derived no-MMU userspace with a tiny native Snakey console UI; standard XFCE4 is not viable on the PSP memory/MMU constraints.
targets.notes: First-wave legacy target. Historical uClinux-on-PSP 0.22 artifacts are documented; source archive, toolchain, kernel patch and licensing must be audited before any build. No current Snakey kernel or hardware boot is claimed.
targets.distribution_strategy: Build a Slackware-compatible MIPS little-endian package/userland adaptation around the historical uClinux no-MMU execution model. Preserve Slackware-style package archives, metadata and pkgtools conventions where they can be ported; standard Slackware/glibc binaries are not ABI-compatible and must not be assumed to run. This is a separate port, not an official Slackware PSP release.
targets.xfce4_notes: PSP's 32 MiB class and no-MMU uClinux lineage rule out a conventional XFCE4/Xorg desktop; use the native micro desktop while retaining Snakey visual identity.
targets.rootfs_strategy: Separate MIPSel no-MMU/uClinux adaptation. Do not feed standard Slackware MIPS/glibc packages into the PSP rootfs; define and validate the ABI/toolchain and package metadata before building a rootfs.

targets.name: Sony PlayStation Vita
targets.toolchain_strategy: ARM hard-float cross-toolchain; pinned upstream Vita build adapter
targets.desktop_goal: Boot the Slackware-compatible userspace and start Snakey Console Desktop based on XFCE4 when the platform graphics, input and memory budget are validated.
targets.notes: First-wave ARM target. Vita Linux Next is pinned for upstream reproduction in CI; this is not a Snakey kernel or a hardware boot.
targets.distribution_strategy: Slackware ARM 15.0 ARMv7-A hard-float minimal rootfs; preserve pkgtools, Slackware package metadata, filesystem layout and SysVinit. 32-bit ARM development ended upstream, so treat this as a compatibility baseline with independent maintenance and Vita-specific rebuilt packages.
targets.xfce4_notes: XFCE4 is the requested desktop, but must be measured on the Vita-specific graphics/input stack before inclusion in an image.
targets.rootfs_strategy: Minimal Slackware-derived root filesystem; kernel/bootloader and console drivers are separate platform layers; Snakey Desktop starts only after Slackware userspace reaches a stable init shell.

targets.name: Sony PlayStation 3
targets.desktop_goal: Boot the Slackware-compatible userspace and start Snakey Console Desktop based on XFCE4 when the platform graphics, input and memory budget are validated.
targets.notes: Mainline Linux v6.12 contains a PS3-specific ps3_defconfig and platform drivers. Snakey now has a pinned upstream kernel build check; boot method, model/firmware compatibility, usable memory, rootfs and hardware boot remain separate validation gates.
targets.toolchain_strategy: PowerPC64 big-endian cross-toolchain; PS3-specific kernel configuration and boot-path audit
targets.distribution_strategy: Slackware-compatible port for this CPU architecture; preserve pkgtools-style package management and Slackware system conventions where upstream support permits
targets.xfce4_notes: XFCE4 is the target; usable memory, boot method, GPU/display support and input drivers must be proven on the exact model.

targets.name: Nintendo Wii
targets.desktop_goal: Boot the Slackware-compatible userspace and start Snakey Console Desktop based on XFCE4 when the platform graphics, input and memory budget are validated.
targets.notes: Historical Wii Linux work; severe memory constraints make a conventional desktop unlikely.
targets.distribution_strategy: Unofficial Slackware-compatible PowerPC32 big-endian port. targets.rootfs_strategy: Minimal Slackware-derived root filesystem; kernel/bootloader and console drivers are separate platform layers; Snakey Desktop starts only after Slackware userspace reaches a stable init shell.

desktop_policy: For PS Vita, Original Xbox and Wii, Snakey Desktop is a Linux userspace session started by the target's Linux init system after the Snakey kernel and root filesystem boot. The initial common backend is a fullscreen software renderer on Linux framebuffer with controller input via evdev; it does not require Xorg or Wayland. Vita may evaluate XFCE4 only after measured resources and drivers. Original Xbox and Wii use the ultra-light Snakey Desktop profile. This is an architecture target, not a claim that these Linux ports or desktops currently boot.
slackware_base_policy: All Linux-capable console ports use Slackware as their distribution base, but not every architecture has an official Slackware release. Use official Slackware package trees where available; otherwise maintain a clearly labeled Slackware-compatible port. Preserve pkgtools/package conventions and SysVinit where feasible. Never label a cross-build as a bootable console image.
